resources.name: Amala Muslim Youth Hopeline (MAS Social Services Foundation)
resources.hours: 6 PM to 10 PM Pacific Time, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday
resources.description: Peer-staffed helpline for Muslim youth, run by volunteers aged 18 to 30 through the MAS Social Services Foundation.
resources.notes: Page gives no age range for callers. Third-party listings show conflicting hours (one gives 9 PM to 1 AM Eastern); official page used. Hours are limited, so pair with 988.

resources.name: American Muslim Health Professionals
resources.description: National nonprofit offering Mental Health First Aid trainings, a mental health toolkit, webinars and a page of Muslim free clinics.
resources.notes: No hotline or therapist directory found on the home page. Contact: contact@amhp.us. Not a crisis resource.

resources.name: Black Men Heal
resources.cost: Selected clients receive 8 free therapy sessions
resources.description: Philadelphia-based nonprofit that connects men of color with therapists of color, weekly virtual groups and gun violence group therapy.
resources.notes: Selection is limited with a likely waitlist. Site says it is not an emergency service. Contact: info@blackmenheal.org. Could also be filed under Black communities.

resources.name: The Loveland Foundation Therapy Fund
resources.cost: Financial assistance for 4 to 12 therapy sessions
resources.description: Fund that helps Black women and nonbinary people pay for therapy and provides a directory of culturally competent therapists.
resources.notes: Application opens quarterly; waitlist email when closed. No phone listed. Page still shows outdated 800-273-TALK crisis wording, so send crisis users to 988 instead.

resources.name: Boris L. Henson Foundation
resources.description: Foundation offering the Let's Talk resource guide of therapists and wellness practitioners for BIPOC communities, plus a school program and resource hubs.
resources.notes: Phone is the foundation's office line, not a helpline. Site redirects from www to http. Cost not stated. Emergency note on site says call 988. Directory at resourceguide.borislhensonfoundation.org.

resources.name: Call BlackLine
resources.description: Peer-support line for Black, Brown, Native and Muslim communities, described by the site as made by and for those communities.
resources.notes: Site is live and lists this number, but states no hours or cost. Call or text may trigger text-message consent. Confirm hours before publishing a claim of 24/7.

resources.name: National Asian American Pacific Islander Mental Health Association (NAAPIMHA)
resources.description: Nonprofit offering trainings, a resource library and policy work on mental health for Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander communities.
resources.notes: No helpline or crisis number on the site. Contact form at naapimha.org/contact-8.

resources.name: DeQH (Desi LGBTQ Helpline for South Asians)
resources.hours: Thursdays and Sundays, 8 PM to 10 PM Eastern; callers can leave a message with safe callback instructions
resources.description: Volunteer helpline for LGBTQ people of South Asian heritage, with limited weekly hours and a callback option.
resources.notes: Limited hours, not a crisis line. Languages not listed on the page. Site name expands to DeQH; confirm full legal name before publishing.

resources.name: NCTSN Refugee Trauma Resources
resources.description: National Child Traumatic Stress Network hub with background, screening guidance and intervention resources on trauma in refugee children and families.
resources.notes: Mostly for clinicians and caregivers. No phone line. Cost 'Free' is inferred from public access; not stated on page.

resources.name: Center for Victims of Torture
resources.description: Nonprofit providing mental health counseling, case management and physiotherapy for torture survivors, most of them refugees or asylum seekers.
resources.notes: Direct care appears centered in Minnesota; the site mentions programs abroad. No phone or cost on the page. See cvt.org/resources/looking-for-care/.

resources.name: The Jed Foundation Mental Health Resource Center
resources.languages: English, Spanish (Crisis Text Line keyword HOLA)
resources.description: Articles and advice for teens and young adults on stress, loneliness, trauma, identity, finding therapy and low-cost care.
resources.notes: Phone and text are the 988 Lifeline and Crisis Text Line as listed on the page, not Jed's own lines. Cost not stated. Languages field is inferred from the HOLA keyword; remove if unwanted.

resources.name: Active Minds
resources.description: Nonprofit that supports student mental health chapters, peer programs and school and youth programming, with crisis links on its site.
resources.notes: Phone and text are 988 and Crisis Text Line as listed on the page. Active Minds has no phone line of its own listed. Crisis page: activeminds.org/crisis-support/.

resources.name: Seize the Awkward
resources.description: Campaign site with videos and conversation starters that help young people check in on friends about mental health.
resources.notes: Footer credits Ad Council, with AFSP and NAMI logos. Operator not stated explicitly. Phone and text are 988 and Crisis Text Line as listed.

resources.name: National Federation of Families
resources.description: Family-run national organization that connects families of children and adults with mental health or substance use needs to family peer support and advocacy.
resources.notes: Phone is the organization's office number, not a helpline. No hours or cost stated. Email ffcmh@ffcmh.org.

resources.name: Give an Hour
resources.description: Nonprofit offering weekly peer support groups, including groups for military, veterans and military families, and trauma-informed trainings.
resources.notes: Site says it does not provide emergency services and gives 988 and text SIGNS to 741741. No provider directory or phone found; cost not stated. Chat tab exists on site but no URL confirmed.

resources.name: Military OneSource Confidential Counseling
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, by phone or secure live chat
resources.description: Department of Defense service offering free short-term non-medical counseling by phone and chat to service members and their families.
resources.notes: Fetched page carried a note that it was a testing site, so re-check on the live public site. Eligibility is on a separate page. Not for veterans after separation beyond limits on that page.

resources.name: Vet Centers (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)
resources.hours: Call center open around the clock
resources.cost: Free; counseling offered at no cost
resources.description: VA community counseling centers for eligible veterans, service members including Guard and Reserve, and families, with a 24-hour call center.
resources.notes: Eligibility criteria are on a separate page. For a crisis, Veterans Crisis Line is dial 988 then press 1 (not confirmed on this page).

resources.name: Institute on Aging Friendship Line
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
resources.languages: English; Cantonese and Mandarin 888-670-2504; Korean 888-560-7684; Spanish 888-571-0411; Tagalog 888-570-0867; Vietnamese 888-670-1361; Russian 888-560-7360
resources.description: Free line for adults 60 and older, adults with disabilities and caregivers who want emotional support, with no need to be in crisis.
resources.notes: Page lists Cantonese and Mandarin under the same number. Institute on Aging Connect is 415-750-4111, 8 AM to 5 PM Pacific, for general questions.

resources.name: Ozone House
resources.description: Youth agency serving ages 10 to 24 and families with a crisis line, shelter, counseling, drop-in meals and housing support.
resources.notes: Hours and text option not stated on page. Drop-in center 734-485-2222 at 102 N. Hamilton, Ypsilanti. Shelter at 1600 N. Huron River Drive, Ypsilanti.

resources.name: SafeHouse Center
resources.hours: 24-hour helpline; lobby open for walk-ins Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 4 PM
resources.cost: Free and confidential for survivors who live, work or were victimized in Washtenaw County
resources.description: Washtenaw County agency providing a 24-hour helpline, emergency shelter, legal advocacy, support groups and crisis counseling for survivors of domestic and sexual violence.
resources.notes: Site has Spanish and Arabic sections. No text or chat listed. Also covers sexual assault, so could be tagged either topic.

resources.name: Corner Health Center
resources.cost: Described as affordable; see site Insurance and Payments page
resources.description: Ypsilanti health center for young people offering mental health care, psychiatry and school-based emotional health programs.
resources.notes: Address 47 N. Huron St, Ypsilanti. Hours and age range not read on the page.

resources.name: Packard Health
resources.hours: Monday to Friday 8 AM to 5 PM, Saturday 8 AM to noon; after-hours answering service
resources.cost: Not stated; federally qualified health center
resources.description: Federally qualified health center offering on-site behavioral health, including evaluation, psychotherapy and psychiatry consultation, in partnership with Washtenaw County CMH.
resources.notes: Page says it cannot accept new adult ADHD patients. Sliding scale not mentioned on this page.

resources.name: NAMI Washtenaw County
resources.hours: Office hours Monday, Tuesday and Thursday, 12 PM to 5 PM
resources.description: Local NAMI affiliate offering support groups, Family-to-Family classes, advocacy and a resource guide.
resources.notes: Office line, not a crisis line. Site lists NAMI HelpLine 1-800-950-6264 (Mon to Fri 10 AM to 6 PM ET) and Washtenaw CMH ACCESS 734-544-3050. Cost not stated. Address 1100 N. Main St, Ann Arbor.

resources.name: Garrett's Space
resources.description: Nonprofit offering free weekly virtual peer support groups and monthly in-person gatherings for young adults aged 18 to 28 with depression, anxiety or suicidal thoughts.
resources.notes: Phone is for community program questions, not crisis. Site directs crises to call or text 988. Hours not stated.

resources.name: Dawn Farm
resources.cost: Not stated; scholarship available for long-term residential treatment
resources.description: Nonprofit providing detox, residential and outpatient addiction treatment, transitional housing, youth and family services and peer support.
resources.notes: No 24-hour line or office hours read on home page. Email info@dawnfarm.org.

resources.name: Home of New Vision
resources.hours: Main office Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM
resources.description: Ann Arbor recovery organization whose care team includes clinicians, mental health staff, peer recovery coaches and case managers.
resources.notes: Address 3115 Professional Dr, Ann Arbor. Specific programs were not listed on the page I read. No 24-hour line stated.

resources.name: Jewish Family Services of Washtenaw County (Thrive Counseling)
resources.hours: Headquarters Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 5 PM, Friday 9 AM to 3 PM
resources.description: Local agency whose Thrive Counseling program accepts appointment requests for counseling.
resources.notes: Phone and hours are for JFS headquarters, not Thrive Counseling specifically. Services, cost and eligibility not described on page. Counseling may serve all faiths; confirm.

resources.name: MSU Center for Survivors
resources.cost: Hotline and advocacy open to anyone in greater Lansing; therapy free for MSU students, faculty and staff; sexual assault healthcare at no cost
resources.description: MSU program providing 24/7 crisis support, advocacy, counseling, relationship violence shelter and a sexual assault healthcare program.
resources.notes: PHONE CONFLICT: the page lists 517-372-6666 as the 24/7 hotline but the footer lists 800-555-0199 (a fictional-range number, possibly a placeholder or tampering). Phone left blank. Verify directly with MSU before publishing. Old URL centerforsurvivors.msu.edu redirects here.

resources.name: HAVEN (Oakland County)
resources.cost: Not stated; insurance not required for forensic nursing exams
resources.description: Oakland County agency with a 24-hour crisis and support line offering intervention, emotional support, information and referrals for domestic and sexual violence.
resources.notes: Anyone may call, including friends and family. Cost of the hotline itself not stated.

resources.name: First Step (Wayne County)
resources.description: Nonprofit serving Wayne County survivors of domestic and sexual violence with a 24-hour helpline, safety planning, advocacy and a support group for male survivors.
resources.notes: Offices in Plymouth (734-416-1111), Wayne (734-722-1772) and Lincoln Park. Mostly western Wayne County, not Detroit city.

resources.name: Turning Point (Macomb County)
resources.cost: Site calls its services free and confidential
resources.description: Macomb County agency with a 24-hour hotline, emergency shelter, counseling, human trafficking support, forensic nurse and legal advocacy.
resources.notes: Office line 586-463-4430. Text option not stated. Also covers sexual assault and human trafficking.

resources.name: YWCA Interim House (Metro Detroit)
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
resources.description: Secure shelter and 24-hour crisis line for women escaping intimate partner violence, with case management, nurse navigation and police-precinct advocates.
resources.notes: Administrative line 313-259-9922. A WXYZ list shows different digits; the official site is used. Serves women only per page.

resources.name: VOICES4 Hotline (Michigan Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence)
resources.description: Statewide hotline for survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence and human trafficking, reachable by phone, text or online chat.
resources.notes: TTY 517-381-8470. Standard text rates may apply. MCEDSV office (517) 347-7000. Chat is started from the 'Start My Chat' link on the page. Resource finder at mcedsv.org/resources/ was not read.

resources.name: Michigan Peer Warmline
resources.hours: 7 days a week, 10 AM to 2 AM (time zone not stated)
resources.cost: Free, regardless of income or insurance
resources.description: Peer-run line staffed by people with lived mental health experience for non-crisis support, with anonymous callers welcome.
resources.notes: Number and hours read on the Common Ground page; the state MiCAL page did not load. State press coverage from 2020 gives the same number and hours. Not a crisis line; use 988 for crisis.

resources.name: NAMI Michigan
resources.description: State NAMI organization offering education programs, peer programs, family support groups and links to local affiliates.
resources.notes: Number appears in the site footer, not labeled as a helpline. Hours and cost not stated. Affiliate finder at nami.org/Affiliate?state=MI.

resources.name: Ruth Ellis Center
resources.description: Highland Park organization serving LGBTQ+ young people through its Young People programs, with a health and wellness center run with Henry Ford Health.
resources.notes: Mental health services were not named on the home page. Address 95 Victor St, Highland Park. An older Metro Times number (313-867-6936) differs; the official site number is used.

resources.name: Southwest Solutions Counseling
resources.description: Detroit nonprofit listing adult, youth and family counseling, early childhood mental health and a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic.
resources.notes: No phone, hours or cost on the page read. See swsol.org/counseling and swsol.org/contact-us. 'MiSide' not confirmed.

resources.name: Hegira Health
resources.description: Western Wayne County behavioral health agency with crisis services, urgent care stabilization and hospital pre-admission reviews.
resources.notes: Page shows two numbers, (734) 793-5026 labeled 1-833-LISTENS and (734) 458-4601, without saying which is the crisis line. Phone left blank. Hours not stated. Based in Westland.

resources.name: Neighborhood Service Organization (360 Neighborhood Wellness Centers)
resources.description: Detroit nonprofit whose 360 Neighborhood Wellness Centers provide behavioral health services at three locations.
resources.notes: Site says the NSO COPE program closed as of Nov 16, 2025 and refers people to DWIHN at 313-833-2500. Hours and cost not stated.

resources.name: American Indian Health and Family Services of Southeast Michigan
resources.hours: Behavioral health Monday to Friday 9 AM to 5 PM; Thursday 10:30 AM to 7 PM
resources.description: Detroit clinic serving American Indian and Alaska Native people and other underserved residents of Southeast Michigan, with behavioral health services.
resources.notes: PHONE UNCLEAR: page lists 313-846-6030 (main), 833-764-5714, 833-764-5715, 313-846-3718 and 833-764-5716 without labeling the behavioral health line. Phone left blank. Address 4559 Wesson, Detroit. Site directs crises to 988.
